== Decipher founder ==

Holland founded Decipher in 1983 in the Norfolk, Virginia area.<ref name="wp-decipher" /> [[Cindy Thornburg]] is a key executive.<ref name="wp-decipher" /> The company grew from a Virginia Tech master's project inspired by a ''Smithsonian'' magazine article on the Beale ciphers. The first product was a puzzle with a $100,000 prize, sold at 50 cents each, with prize insurance through Lloyd's of London.<ref name="worlds-special" />

Decipher's path into licensed games ran through Pente Games to Parker Brothers, where Holland met [[Tom Braunlich]] and [[Rollie Tesh]]. The company took a ''Star Wars'' license and a side license with Parker Brothers for a two-player game. The first guarantee was $1 million.<ref name="worlds-special" />

== Star Wars license and production ==

For card images, Decipher had access to Lucas archives and a duplicate 70mm print of the original trilogy. Holland hired a German film editor for $80,000 for frame-by-frame high-resolution scans. A later Lucas encyclopedia used about one-third of Decipher's images. Work at Skywalker Ranch included being one of two licenses allowed to take the Episode I script off the ranch. For Special Edition characters who were not in the original film, Decipher hired a local theater company and actors.<ref name="worlds-special" /><ref name="ringer" />

Holland's interest in Joseph Campbell's hero's journey led to the game's split into Light Side and Dark Side.<ref name="bp-campbell">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc&t=535s The Booster Pack #28 — The making of the Star Wars CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (24 August 2022), 8:55–10:00. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20221006131758/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[The Booster Pack/Episode 28 transcript]].</ref> Through 1995 he reviewed every proposed card in the design team's evening sessions and passed none he did not love.<ref name="bp-sessions">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc&t=1283s The Booster Pack #28 — The making of the Star Wars CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (24 August 2022), 21:23–23:57. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20221006131758/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[The Booster Pack/Episode 28 transcript]].</ref> Former staffer [[Jason Winter]] recalled that Holland sat in on design meetings and preferred balancing cards through design rather than banned lists or copy limits. Holland also bought a house near the office for product development.<ref name="winter">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aq_dwh8Ojys&t=1091s Inside the Star Wars CCG: Secrets from Decipher], Imperial Remnant (23 November 2025), at 18:11. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261015165322/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aq_dwh8Ojys Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Inside the Star Wars CCG: Secrets from Decipher (transcript)]].</ref>

== Players Committee ==

On 28 December 2001 Holland announced that Lucasfilm would not renew Decipher's ''Star Wars'' CCG license. Sell-off ran through 30 April 2002.<ref name="rfd-sb">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZpXfkPyurfE&t=3s Radio Free Decipher Special Broadcast (28 December, 2001): Warren Holland and the Players Committee], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 18 February 2022), at 00:03. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZpXfkPyurfE Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Special Broadcast (28 December 2001) transcript]].</ref> He said the relationship with Lucasfilm had been good until Hasbro bought Wizards of the Coast. He had recently settled legal issues with Lucasfilm over its handling of the license.<ref name="rfd-sb-hasbro">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZpXfkPyurfE&t=183s Radio Free Decipher Special Broadcast (28 December, 2001): Warren Holland and the Players Committee], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 18 February 2022), at 03:03. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZpXfkPyurfE Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Special Broadcast (28 December 2001) transcript]].</ref> Decipher's offer to keep the license was the largest it had made for any license. Hasbro, he said, had convinced Lucasfilm it could double sales with a younger, ''Pokémon''-style audience.<ref name="rfd-sb-offer">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZpXfkPyurfE&t=282s Radio Free Decipher Special Broadcast (28 December, 2001): Warren Holland and the Players Committee], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 18 February 2022), at 04:42. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZpXfkPyurfE Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Special Broadcast (28 December 2001) transcript]].</ref> ''Star Wars'' Second Edition and digital cards would have launched in 2001 had Lucasfilm approved them.<ref name="rfd-sb-se">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZpXfkPyurfE&t=756s Radio Free Decipher Special Broadcast (28 December, 2001): Warren Holland and the Players Committee], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 18 February 2022), at 12:36. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZpXfkPyurfE Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Special Broadcast (28 December 2001) transcript]].</ref> The cancellation of DecipherCon 2001 had nothing to do with the license.<ref name="rfd-sb-con">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZpXfkPyurfE&t=910s Radio Free Decipher Special Broadcast (28 December, 2001): Warren Holland and the Players Committee], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 18 February 2022), at 15:10. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZpXfkPyurfE Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Special Broadcast (28 December 2001) transcript]].</ref> Decipher's first ''Lord of the Rings'' expansion had already outsold every SWCCG expansion of the previous four years.<ref name="rfd-sb-lotr">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZpXfkPyurfE&t=1015s Radio Free Decipher Special Broadcast (28 December, 2001): Warren Holland and the Players Committee], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 18 February 2022), at 16:55. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZpXfkPyurfE Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Special Broadcast (28 December 2001) transcript]].</ref>

On that broadcast he announced the [[Players Committee]].<ref name="rfd-sb-pc">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZpXfkPyurfE&t=1332s Radio Free Decipher Special Broadcast (28 December, 2001): Warren Holland and the Players Committee], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 18 February 2022), at 22:12. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZpXfkPyurfE Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Special Broadcast (28 December 2001) transcript]].</ref><ref name="pc-hist">[[History of the Players Committee]]</ref> On 25 January 2002 he named the first six Player Advocates.<ref name="pc-adv" /><ref name="wp-swccg" /> Decipher donated $1 million of SWCCG inventory, with royalties to Lucasfilm prepaid, for the committee to use as prizes.<ref name="ringer" />

== Later games ==

[[Bill Martinson]] said on ''[[Radio Free Decipher]]'' in April 1999 that [[Young Jedi]] was Holland's conception. Holland was closely involved in its gameplay and card design.<ref name="rfd13">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XvKFYzu0P-k&t=51s Broadcast 13 - Radio Free Decipher (09 April, 1999): Bill Martinson, Jerry Darcy on PD (Part 2)], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 20 February 2022), at 00:51. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-XvKFYzu0P-k Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 13 transcript]].</ref>

Holland is credited on Decipher's [[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game]] team. Designer [[Chuck Kallenbach]] said Holland asked him and [[Tom Lischke]] to "do something different" with the planned classic-trilogy version of Young Jedi, which became Jedi Knights.<ref name="jkrules">[http://www.decipher.com/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt ''Jedi Knights'' Trading Card Game rulebook (credits)], Decipher (2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010820125115/http://www.decipher.com:80/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="tfnck">Josh Radke, [http://www.theforce.net/ccg/flashback/article.asp Flashback: Chuck Kallenbach interview], TheForce.Net. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261010072858/http://www.theforce.net/ccg/flashback/article.asp Internet Archive]</ref>

In 2004 the ''Star Wars'' CCG mechanics returned in [[WARS TCG]], an original science-fiction property. Holland said a sci-fi setting with movement in space was "almost dictated" by the mechanics, and that building the universe around the game made for stronger science fiction.<ref name="wars3">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lxL-5bskkaw&t=185s Ep. 3 - Decipher WARS Radio (09 July, 2004): Warren Holland Interview; What's Happening in Art], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 15 May 2022), at 03:05. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-lxL-5bskkaw Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[WARS Radio/Episode 3 transcript]].</ref>

== Interviews ==

=== Radio Free Decipher, 5 October 2001 ===
After cancelling DecipherCon 2001, Holland went on ''[[Radio Free Decipher]]'' Broadcast 99 to answer players' questions. He said safety was the only reason for the decision. He compared the convention to a party on a barge offshore after shark sightings. Most swimmers would be safe, but the company should not ask everyone to swim out.<ref name="rfd99-barge">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wS84wdG4EUI&t=242s Broadcast 99 - Radio Free Decipher (05 October, 2001): Warren Holland on DecipherCon and 9/11], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 13 May 2022), at 04:02. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-wS84wdG4EUI Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 99 transcript]].</ref> He said he had personally answered about 50 emails at ceo@decipher.com and that the qualified players would choose charities for the prize money.<ref name="rfd99-email">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wS84wdG4EUI&t=49s Broadcast 99 - Radio Free Decipher (05 October, 2001): Warren Holland on DecipherCon and 9/11], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 13 May 2022), at 00:49. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-wS84wdG4EUI Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 99 transcript]].</ref>

=== Radio Free Decipher special broadcast, 28 December 2001 ===
Holland announced the license end and the [[Players Committee]] on a Radio Free Decipher special broadcast.<ref name="rfd-sb" /><ref name="rfd-sb-pc" />

=== WARS Radio, July 2004 ===
Holland explained why the SWCCG mechanics returned in [[WARS TCG]] on two July 2004 episodes of Decipher ''[[WARS Radio]]''.<ref name="wars3" /><ref name="wars4">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FWBYRjMvhZw&t=569s Ep. 4 - Decipher WARS Radio (16 July, 2004): Holland Interview Part 2 and a Gongen Big Reveal!], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 15 May 2022), at 09:29. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261012022823/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FWBYRjMvhZw&pp=iAQB Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[WARS Radio/Episode 4 transcript]].</ref>

=== NanashiStudios, 14 June 2026 ===
Holland recounted Decipher's founding and the ''Star Wars'' license in the 2025 SWCCG Worlds Special, speaking from about 3:05.<ref name="worlds-special" />
